journal_name: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition

abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework that fundamentally reconceptualizes how document structure is represented through hierarchical graph neural networks. Traditional document analysis approaches typically process textual content and layout information in isolated pipelines, fundamentally limiting their capacity to capture intrinsic document semantics. We propose a unified representation paradigm where document elements are modeled as nodes in a heterogeneous graph, with edges encoding multi-dimensional relationships including spatial proximity, semantic similarity, and typographical hierarchy. The core theoretical contribution lies in the derivation of a new message-passing mechanism that enables dynamic feature propagation across modality boundaries, eliminating the need for explicit modality alignment. We mathematically prove that this framework satisfies permutation invariance properties essential for robust document understanding. Experimental validation on benchmark datasets for document layout analysis and text detection demonstrates that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance while requiring fewer parameters than competing methods. This work represents a paradigm shift from component-wise document processing toward holistic graph-based interpretation, opening new research directions for document intelligence.

We present a theoretically grounded approach to improving handwriting recognition accuracy through adaptive contextual modeling. While contemporary sequence-to-sequence models have advanced handwritten text recognition significantly, they often fail to adequately capture long-range dependencies within variable writing styles. This paper derives a novel attention mechanism based on Bayesian decision theory that dynamically weights character-level features according to their discriminative power within specific writing contexts. The theoretical analysis reveals that previous attention models suffer from a fundamental limitation: they treat positional encoding and content-based attention as independent processes, whereas our unified formulation optimizes both jointly. We further establish theoretical bounds demonstrating that the proposed mechanism reduces overfitting on rare character combinations by approximately 23% compared to standard attention. Empirical evaluation on IAM and RIMES datasets confirms that the theoretically motivated design yields substantial improvements in word-level accuracy, particularly for historical documents exhibiting high writing variability. This work provides both principled theoretical foundations and practical algorithmic advances for handwriting recognition systems.

This paper introduces an end-to-end document processing system that fundamentally reimagines the integration of layout analysis and text recognition through a unified vision-language architecture. Unlike conventional pipelines that treat page segmentation and optical character recognition as separate stages, our system employs a single transformer-based backbone that simultaneously performs text detection, layout analysis, and character recognition in a fully differentiable manner. The architectural innovation centers on a novel cross-modal attention module that enables real-time information flow between visual features and language representations, eliminating information bottlenecks inherent in cascaded systems. We design a hierarchical tokenization scheme that preserves both fine-grained character details and document-level structural semantics. The complete system achieves F1 scores of 0.94 on document layout analysis and character error rates below 1.8% on complex mixed-content documents, surpassing previous multi-stage approaches while reducing inference time by 60%. This unified architecture represents a paradigm shift toward joint optimization of document understanding tasks, providing a scalable foundation for next-generation document intelligence applications.

We present an efficient handwritten document recognition system specifically optimized for deployment on mobile and edge devices with limited computational resources. The system architecture combines a lightweight convolutional feature extractor with an optimized recurrent decoder, achieving a favorable trade-off between recognition accuracy and computational efficiency. Key design contributions include a novel feature compression module that reduces intermediate representations by 40% while preserving essential discriminative information, and a dynamic vocabulary prediction mechanism that adapts output character sets based on document context. We implement the system using quantization-aware training and develop custom kernel implementations for ARM-based processors, enabling real-time processing at 15 frames per second on consumer smartphones. Extensive evaluation across diverse handwritten document collections demonstrates that the system maintains recognition accuracy above 95% while operating within strict resource constraints. For form processing applications, the system achieves processing throughput improvements of 3.2x compared to existing mobile solutions, making practical mobile document digitization commercially viable.
